🌉 Central San Francisco, every building standing today by year of construction — 1860 → 2025.

On 18 April 1906, an earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed most of the city east of Van Ness Avenue. The Victorian neighbourhoods to the west and south survived, which is why they still glow orange. The burnt centre was rebuilt in under a decade, the Sunset and the Richmond filled with row houses between the 1920s and the 1950s, and the towers of the Financial District rose after 1960.

📊 Data: DataSF, Assessor tax roll 2025 and building footprints (PDDL). 85% of years come from the tax roll; 15% are estimated: the placeholder year 1900 is spread block by block over 1870–1905 (1906–1925 inside the area burnt in 1906), or the year of neighbouring buildings. Landmarks keep their known year. Heights exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
